scope: read-only source review of L4 ENOSPC and directly called helpers; no test, PostgreSQL, Docker, mount, process or service execution
verdict: P2 fixture timing race; no P1 found; no guaranteed deterministic production API mismatch established

findings.title: The live worker can advance past the failed operation before physical pressure is removed
evidence: l4 starts the actual worker, approves the original command, then leaves that worker running throughout pressure creation, SQLite observation, PostgreSQL capture and Docker inspection.

application.Driver.operation inspects every 100ms. Once its local runner execution ends, Engine.InspectOperation may reconcile the stopped job and publish an incomplete bounded log prefix as a terminal failed receipt, even while the separate pressure file remains.

The scripted next model round is an immediately executable apply_patch. It may encounter ENOSPC before releasePressure(), after which finishDriver still requires completed. Alternatively a yielded/reclaimed worker can adopt at a newer workspace epoch while f.settle(req) continues using the original request epoch and fails fenced.

The test-only comment that it reads SQLite rather than Inspect does not prevent the real worker from calling Inspect. No coordination barrier currently orders all application advancement after pressure removal.
findings.impact: A valid conservative runner outcome can make this acceptance test fail nondeterministically; this is not a demonstrated production data-loss bug or proof that every actual run will fail.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a bounded explicit fixture coordination point that prevents the live worker from executing the dependent repair until pressure removal and original-operation receipt observation are complete, while preserving the original operation identity. A separately approved next tool can provide such a gate. Do not weaken production fencing or force synthetic lease expiry.

checked_contracts.physical_target: pressure(filepath.Dir(spool)) resolves to workspace-<id>/strict-logs-enospc-pressure, outside the task checkout and logs directory. spoolPath binds tenant/run/workspace to the persisted slot. All four actual volume identities are verified in fixture and production runner preflight.
checked_contracts.bounded_allocation: O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW mode0600; writes at most256MiB and requires actual ENOSPC; records device/inode/statfs/allocated bytes. Before deletion verifies inode,device,link count,owner.
checked_contracts.retention: No deferred pressure deletion. Explicit removal follows exact original container ID/label/mount oracle with running=false, original log reservation unchanged and released=0. Failure finalize stops only fixture-owned processes and leaves pressure/unknown workspace/SQL records.
checked_contracts.restore: After removal, Inspect uses the same operation ID. The production reader allows a checksum-validated prefix with absent metadata and explicitly incomplete capture, then publication and cleanup can proceed. This is subject to the live-worker ordering race above.
checked_contracts.publication: captureOperation compares durable request/status/job/result/receipt, opens hash/length-checked pinned log and receipt artifacts, compares actual disk prefix, and checks original container identity. L4 waits for PG READY then uses the administrator-scoped fixture Store for authenticated HTTP checks.
checked_contracts.cleanup: finishDriver requires completed then invokes production CleanupWorkspace, requiring sealed snapshot before release; volume identities are rechecked and a fresh actual health operation proves slot reuse.
checked_contracts.non_blocking_hardening: pressure records st_dev but does not itself explicitly compare it against the selected slot/checkout immediately before writing. Existing path derivation, initial no-symlink spool read and volume preflights establish the intended scope under an unchanged trusted fixture. Rechecking the selected VolumeSpec and comparing open fd st_dev to slot/checkout would make the physical pressure boundary more directly reviewable.

not_claimed: No real ENOSPC or lifecycle result observed by this review
No guaranteed repeatable failure proved without execution
No source change or new feature implemented
